title: UK Director Liquidation, Part 1 of 3: Using AI to Beat the Red Tape

scenes.label: HOOK
scenes.title: Hook
scenes.broll: Goal image, slow push-in. No figures on screen
scenes.vo: My company is coming to an end, and I'm closing it properly. If you're a UK director in the same spot, here's how a liquidation works, and the five things to do first.

scenes.label: INTRO
scenes.title: Part 1 of 3: AI and real-world red tape
scenes.vo: I'm Rifat, from Cambridge. This is Part 1 of three: using AI to get through real-world red tape. It's time to say goodbye to this company, and doing the numbers is a hassle. And you don't want to make a mistake you'd regret.
overlay: Don't make a mistake you'd regret
scenes.ph: Face cam placeholder · lower-third: Rifat · Cambridge, UK

scenes.label: CHAPTER 1
scenes.title: The goal
scenes.broll: Goal infographic, the three-step process highlighted
scenes.vo: Here's the goal. Company debt stays the company's. A licensed practitioner takes over, sells the assets and pays creditors in order. There's a lot of red tape in society, so understand it first.
overlay: 1 Hand over  →  2 Sell assets  →  3 Pay creditors in order
Lots of red tape: understand it first

scenes.label: CHAPTER 2
scenes.title: Five things to do first, with AI
scenes.broll: On-screen numbered list 1 to 5. Optional HMRC screen inset for step 1 (S2), UTR, login and balance hidden
scenes.vo: Five things to do first, with AI as your support. Every time I'm on the HMRC site, I leave with more questions than answers, so I ask AI to explain each step before I act. One: check your HMRC balance. Two: gather the company's books and records. Three: get a licensed insolvency practitioner. I chose one with 4.8 stars on Trustpilot. Four: stop trading, and don't pay one creditor ahead of the others. Your practitioner will confirm this. Five: close your invoices and bring every bank account to zero, or the money goes to the Crown.
overlay: Use AI to get through the red tape
scenes.ph: Optional: HMRC screen (S2) inset for step 1. Blur UTR + login, hide the balance

scenes.label: CHAPTER 3
scenes.title: What it costs and how long it takes
scenes.broll: Cost and timeline graphic: £1,500 + £2,100, five stages, Gazette wait
scenes.vo: Here's what it costs: a £1,500 deposit, then a £2,100 balance. I've paid both, and the process takes about two months. Don't try to do it with AI alone. Learn the process, delegate with AI, and still use a professional. Using AI gives you leverage, so use it on processes like this to get better at AI, not just to finish one. The skills you learn here carry over to your next project.
overlay: Get better at AI, not just the process

scenes.label: CHAPTER 4
scenes.title: The exceptions
scenes.broll: Four exception cards on screen, red accent
scenes.vo: Now the exceptions, because this matters. The protection isn't absolute. A director can still be personally liable for wrongful or fraudulent trading, personal guarantees, an overdrawn director's loan account, or paying one creditor first. That's why the practitioner decides. Understand the basics, because even the people closest to you won't get what you're really doing. And keep your expectations of AI low: it gives you the courage and the assist you need. Most people get stuck in red tape and can't move.
overlay: Low expectations of AI: it gives you courage and the assist

scenes.label: CHAPTER 5
scenes.title: What my emails taught me
scenes.broll: Email timeline graphic (S12): chase reminders, the receipt (names and addresses blurred), then a simple diagram of Gmail and Drive connected to AI over MCP
scenes.vo: Three lessons from my own emails. One: the process stops until the balance is paid, and my provider chased me six times. Two: answer everything in writing, and keep a list of what's still outstanding. Three: treat Google Drive and Gmail as data sources, and get ready to connect them to AI over MCP, instead of sending everything by hand. From time to time things will go wrong. Learn from them, and iterate.
overlay: 2 Answer in writing, list what is outstanding
3 Gmail + Drive as data sources, over MCP

scenes.label: CHAPTER 6
scenes.title: How I keep track of it
scenes.broll: n8n canvas, 20 seconds (S3), then the dashboard (S10)
scenes.vo: I keep track of it all with an n8n workflow and a few AI agents: a planner, a risk checker and a director. Divide and conquer is the key. Even if people make fun of you for it, use that as a learning tool, and build your system and mindset for your next role.
